title: Conflict test vs view test
misconception: Treating CSR as the definition of serializability: a conflict cycle does not rule out VSR (blind writes).

transcript.text: Your reasoning treated the conflict test as the definition of serializability. Let's pull the two ideas apart.

View-serializability asks: same reads and same final writes as some serial schedule? Conflict-serializability is stricter: the same order on every conflicting pair. Every CSR schedule is VSR; the converse is not necessarily true.

Look at this schedule. T2 and T1 write x without reading it first: these are blind writes. Their order creates conflicts in both directions, yet nobody ever reads what they wrote, because T3 overwrites x at the end.
Against the serial order T1, T2, T3: T1 reads the initial x and T3 writes last, in both. So what does a conflict cycle really tell you? Try the next question yourself.
